chunks: If the foundation on which it is borne and the stones with which it is raised were of green emerald and red ruby, and [filled with] light and brightness,

then this would have lessened the action of doubts in the breasts, would have dismissed the effect of Satan’s striving from the hearts, and would have removed the surging of misgivings from the people.
But Allah, Glorified is He, tests His servants with various hardships, makes them worship through different struggles, and tries them with various adversities,
to extract arrogance from their hearts, to settle humility in their souls, and to make that an open door to His bounty and an easy means for His forgiveness.
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah choose simple materials for the Kaaba instead of precious gems?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the hypothetical splendor of the Kaaba with its actual humble stone structure, arguing that simplicity serves as a greater test of faith than visual grandeur. This perspective highlights the Shia scholarly view that divine wisdom lies in using material austerity to combat human arrogance (takabbur) and cultivate true humility (tadhallul), thereby turning trials into pathways for divine grace.

en.sayed-ali-raza: If the foundation on which the House is borne and the stones with which it has been raised had been of green emerald and red rubies, and there had been brightness and effulgence,
then this would have lessened the action of doubts in the breasts, would have dismissed the effect of Satan’s activity from the hearts, and would have stopped the surging of misgivings in people.
But Allāh tries His creatures by means of different troubles, wants them to render worship through hardships and involves them in distresses,

all in order to extract out vanity from their hearts, to settle down humbleness in their spirits and to make all this an open door for His favours and an easy means for His forgiveness (for their sins).
